The charcoal rot and fusarium references show stem/root-level symptoms, not the field-level yellowing pattern seen in the test image.

The test image shows a soybean field with distinctive **circular/lens-shaped patches of yellowing** plants scattered among otherwise healthy green plants. This field-level symptom pattern is the hallmark of Soybean Cyst Nematode (SCN), which the symptom description confirms: "yellowing of leaves, stunting of plants, and early maturity, commonly appearing in circular or lens-shaped patterns in the field." The SCN reference collage (bottom-right quadrant) shows a very similar field-level view with patchy yellowing.

While SDS can also cause field patches, SDS typically shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis on individual leaves with green veins, and the SDS reference's field view shows more linear/row patterns rather than the rounded, scattered patches seen here.

The patchy, irregular distribution of chlorotic plants matches the SCN symptom description of yellowing appearing in circular or lens-shaped patterns."}
